title: Battle of Lwów
summary: The term 'Battle of Lwów' refers to several significant military engagements that occurred in and around the city of Lwów (now Lviv, [[ukraine|Ukraine]]), highlighting its strategic importance throughout various historical conflicts.

sections.heading: Early Conflicts
paragraphs: The Battle of Lwów in 1675 marked a confrontation where Ottoman forces were defeated by Polish troops led by John III Sobieski.
Another notable engagement, the Battle of Lwów in 1695, saw Ottoman armies again defeated, this time by Hussars under the command of [[hetman|hetman]] Stanisław Jan Jabłonowski.

sections.heading: Great Northern War and World War I
paragraphs: During the Great Northern War, the Storming of Lemberg in 1704 resulted in the capture and looting of Lwów by Swedish forces.
In World War I, the Battle of Lemberg in 1914, also known as the Battle of [[galicia|Galicia]], led to the capture of Lemberg by Russian troops at the war's outset.
The following year, in 1915, [[lviv|Lviv]] was recaptured by Austria-Hungary during another battle involving the 4th Division.

sections.heading: Post-World War I Conflicts
paragraphs: The Battle of Lemberg in 1918 involved urban combat between local Polish residents and the forces of the [[west-ukrainian-peoples-republic|West Ukrainian People's Republic]], reflecting the region's complex national dynamics.
In 1920, the Battle of Lwów consisted of several weeks of fighting at the city's outskirts between the Polish Army and the Red Army during the Polish–Bolshevik War.

sections.heading: World War II Engagements
paragraphs: The Battle of Lwów in 1939 was characterized by a siege of the city by German forces during the Invasion of Poland, leading to its capitulation to the Soviet Union.
In 1941, Lwów fell to German troops in another significant engagement during World War II.
The Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive in 1944 represented a Soviet campaign against German forces, while the Lwów Uprising later that year involved the Polish Home Army and Soviet forces capturing the city.
